title: GitHub Actions workflows: read a PR's linked issues with gh api graphql using typed -F variables and a --jq filter
answers: How do I get the issue numbers a pull request closes from inside a workflow step?
How do I call the GraphQL API with gh in a workflow with owner and repo variables?
Why does my gh api graphql query fail on the number argument?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml, step "Comment on linked issues" in job comment-on-linked-issues. This is the pattern for running a GraphQL query from a workflow step to read a PR's linked issues (closingIssuesReferences) before acting on them.
Rule: Pass owner and number with -F so they are typed (Int for number), and pass the query text with -f. Derive the repo name with ${REPO#*/} from github.repository, since the GraphQL call needs owner and name separately. Filter the output with --jq '.data.repository.pullRequest.closingIssuesReferences.nodes[].number' and loop over the lines with a for loop.
Constraints: Use GH_TOKEN from secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN; the token needs pull-requests: read to query and issues: write to comment. Results are capped by first: N in the query (the PR uses 10).
applies: Applies to GitHub Actions steps in this repo that need PR-to-issue linkage data; not needed for REST-only calls.
says: Find all issues linked to a pull request during automated workflow runs.
Automatically post comments to tickets closed by a pull request when it merges.
Querying linked issues in an automated pull request task fails on number arguments.
Identify the issues referenced by a pull request to perform follow-up actions.
search: Workflow steps querying linked pull request issues with `gh api graphql` must pass typed variables using `-F` and query strings with `-f`. In `.github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml`, the `comment-on-linked-issues` job queries `closingIssuesReferences`, splits `github.repository` into owner and repo with `${REPO#*/}`, and filters output with `--jq '.data.repository.pullRequest.closingIssuesReferences.nodes[].number'`. The step requires `GH_TOKEN` from `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` with permissions `pull-requests: read` and `issues: write`, with results limited by `first: N`.
